question: Why must a patient not eat or drink (remain NPO) for several hours before ECT?

options.A: To lower their resting blood pressure
options.B: To prevent aspiration under anesthesia
options.C: To make the electrical current work faster
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling nervous

explanation: Patients receive general anesthesia during ECT, making an empty stomach essential to prevent inhaling stomach contents into the lungs. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T5#BMP223_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is teamwork between different health agencies important for midwives in clinical and community practice?

options.A: No single health agency has all the resources to solve every community health problem alone
options.B: It allows nurses to avoid clinical duties by passing patients to administrative staff
options.C: Government regulations mandate that every nurse must run an independent NGO
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient consent during health outreaches

explanation: Healthcare is complex, and sharing resources between government bodies, NGOs, and hospitals ensures patients get complete support. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T7#BMP110_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is a concealed abruption so dangerous?

options.A: Fetal distress is completely impossible with concealed blood
options.B: Blood loss is hidden, leading to delayed shock recognition
options.C: It never causes any pain or discomfort for the mother
options.D: It only occurs during the third stage of normal labor

explanation: Because the bleeding stays inside the uterus, it is easy to underestimate the total blood loss and miss early signs of shock. [learn more](BMP221_U2_T3#BMP221_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering vasopressors like norepinephrine during shock?

options.A: To constrict blood vessels and raise blood pressure
options.B: To lower the patient's heart rate to a normal rhythm
options.C: To thin the blood and prevent dangerous clots
options.D: To put the patient into a deep sleep for surgery

explanation: Vasopressors tighten widened blood vessels, which helps push blood pressure back up to safe levels. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T5#BMP120_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which side effect of routine iron supplements should midwives explain to clients so they do not stop taking them?

options.A: Dark stools
options.B: Blurred vision
options.C: Rapid weight gain
options.D: Hair loss

explanation: Unabsorbed iron commonly turns the stool a harmless dark or black color, which can alarm patients if they are not warned beforehand. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h4)

question: Which type of nosocomial infection is most directly linked to the use of an indwelling urethral tube?

options.A: Surgical Site Infection
options.B: Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection
options.C: Primary Bloodstream Infection
options.D: Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia

explanation: Any infection of the urinary tract related to a catheter in place is classified specifically as a CAUTI. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T3#BMP116_U5_T3_h2)

question: How do humans primarily become infected with this parasite?

options.A: Direct skin contact with infected soil while farming
options.B: Ingesting food or water contaminated with cysts
options.C: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes during the rainy season
options.D: Inhaling airborne spores released from dry soil

explanation: Transmission happens via the fecal-oral route when a person swallows food or water polluted with microscopic cysts. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T5#BMP116_U3_T5_h2)

question: How do Staphylococcus bacteria usually enter the breast tissue to cause postpartum mastitis?

options.A: Hormonal changes after delivering the placenta
options.B: Blocked milk ducts from tight bras
options.C: Drinking too much fluid during labor
options.D: Cracked or sore nipples

explanation: Breaks in the skin of the nipple during early breastfeeding provide a direct pathway for skin bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus to enter breast tissue. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which hormone does a standard pregnancy test strip check for?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estriol
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Pregnancy tests are designed to identify the presence of human chorionic gonadotropin in maternal urine or blood. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T2#BMP212_U1_T2_h5)

question: What texture is best for a baby starting solid foods at six months?

options.A: Thick mashes and smooth purees
options.B: Dry biscuits and large chunks of meat
options.C: Whole hard nuts and raw carrots
options.D: Completely watery liquids only

explanation: Thick mashes make it easy to transition from liquids while providing more nutrients than watery porridges. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h4)

question: A midwifery school has zero budget for expensive computerized manikins. How can the educator still run effective simulation sessions?

options.A: Cancel all practical teaching until government funding arrives
options.B: Wait for students to graduate before teaching them clinical skills
options.C: Rely entirely on reading textbooks without any physical practice
options.D: Use locally improvised low-cost models and peer-led role-play

explanation: Faculty creativity, low-cost local materials, and role-play can successfully substitute for expensive high-tech simulators. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T8#BMP312_U3_T8_h6)

question: A mother says her 10-month-old child refuses to finish a large bowl of thin, watery pap. What practical advice should you give?

options.A: Stop giving solid food entirely and return to exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Add more water to the pap so it is easier for the infant to swallow
options.C: Make the pap thicker and enrich it with mashed beans or groundnut paste in a smaller bowl
options.D: Force-feed the child using a spoon until the entire bowl of watery pap is finished

explanation: Thick, nutrient-rich foods provide more energy in fewer bites, which fits a baby's small stomach capacity. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T4#BMP227_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is addressing psychosocial wellbeing considered part of a healthy school environment?

options.A: Teachers are legally classified as psychological counselors
options.B: It prevents physical infectious diseases from spreading among students
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of building maintenance for the school
options.D: Emotional safety and freedom from bullying directly affect learning and mental health

explanation: A safe psychosocial climate protects students from trauma and stress, creating an atmosphere conducive to academic growth. [learn more](BMP126_U3_T1#BMP126_U3_T1_h5)

question: How does the typical appetite of a child with marasmus compare to one with kwashiorkor?

options.A: Kwashiorkor children eat voraciously while marasmus children lose interest
options.B: Both groups of children refuse all forms of food completely
options.C: Marasmus children are usually hungry; kwashiorkor children are anoretic
options.D: Neither condition has any impact on the child's daily appetite

explanation: Children with marasmus are typically alert and hungry, whereas kwashiorkor patients suffer from severe anorexia and lack interest in food. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T2#BMP118_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of percussing the abdomen?

options.A: To determine if underlying organs contain air, fluid, or solid tissue
options.B: To check for skin temperature variations across different quadrants
options.C: To stimulate sluggish peristalsis in patients with constipation
options.D: To measure the exact blood pressure inside the portal vein

explanation: Percussion produces different tones (like tympany or dullness) that reveal whether underlying structures are hollow or solid. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T1#BMP125_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which Nigerian regulatory body defines the legal scope of practice for midwives?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for setting training standards and defining the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h3)

question: About how many extra daily calories does a woman need while exclusively breastfeeding?

options.A: About 2000 calories
options.B: No extra calories are needed
options.C: About 500 calories
options.D: About 100 calories

explanation: Milk production requires substantial energy, leading to an increased daily caloric requirement for the mother. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which major hormonal shift occurs immediately after delivery that contributes to biological vulnerability for mood changes?

options.A: A sharp drop in estrogen and progesterone
options.B: A total shutdown of the pituitary gland
options.C: An abrupt increase in circulating testosterone
options.D: A massive permanent surge in cortisol levels

explanation: The sudden withdrawal of pregnancy hormones like estrogen and progesterone heavily influences brain chemistry and mood regulation after childbirth. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T1#BMP223_U3_T1_h3)

question: What microscopic arrangement is characteristic of Staphylococcus species?

options.A: Grape-like clusters
options.B: Flagellated spirals
options.C: Pairs of kidney-shaped cells
options.D: Chains of round cells

explanation: Staphylococcus bacteria divide in multiple planes, which causes them to clump together in irregular shapes that resemble bunches of grapes under the microscope. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T3#BMP116_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which strains of HPV are most commonly linked to cervical cancer?

options.A: HPV types 6 and 11
options.B: HPV types 30 and 32
options.C: HPV types 50 and 52
options.D: HPV types 16 and 18

explanation: Strains 16 and 18 are high-risk types responsible for the majority of cervical cancers worldwide. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T11#BMP310_U2_T11_h1)

question: What does objectivity mean in the context of quantitative research?

options.A: The findings change depending on who is reading the final report.
options.B: The personal opinions of the researcher do not alter the data results.
options.C: The participants choose which questions they prefer to answer.
options.D: The study focuses exclusively on subjective emotional feelings.

explanation: Objectivity ensures that measurements and findings remain neutral and unbiased by personal feelings. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T2#BMP225_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of antimicrobial stewardship programs in healthcare?

options.A: Replacing all injectable medications with oral syrups and tablets
options.B: Promoting the safe, appropriate, and effective use of anti-infective drugs
options.C: Reducing the financial cost of hospital building maintenance and cleaning
options.D: Ensuring that every patient admitted to the ward receives prophylactic drugs

explanation: Stewardship helps ensure drugs are used correctly to get the best clinical results while preventing side effects and slowing down drug resistance. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h4)

question: A pregnant woman presents with rapid weight loss, severe tremors, and a racing heart despite eating well. Which condition should you suspect?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Adrenal insufficiency
options.C: Hyperthyroidism
options.D: Hypothyroidism

explanation: Rapid weight loss, tremors, and a fast heart rate are classic signs of an overactive thyroid gland producing excess thyroid hormones. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T1#BMP216_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why do newborn babies wet themselves constantly without conscious control?

options.A: The micturition reflex is purely spinal and lacks adult higher brain modulation
options.B: The kidneys produce too much urine relative to body size
options.C: The external urethral sphincter is permanently paralyzed in infants
options.D: The detrusor muscle lacks the ability to contract on its own

explanation: Infant nervous systems are not yet fully matured, meaning the brain cannot yet override the basic spinal reflex that empties the bladder automatically. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which local group brings community leaders, health workers, and agricultural agents together in Nigeria?

options.A: Midwives Board of Nigeria
options.B: Ward Development Committee
options.C: Federal Ministry of Finance
options.D: National Medical Association

explanation: Ward Development Committees are designed to engage multiple community stakeholders in planning and supporting primary health care. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T6#BMP117_U1_T6_h6)

question: A laboratory scientist forgets to add the decolorizer step during a Gram stain. What will most bacteria look like under the microscope?

options.A: All bacteria will appear pink or red
options.B: No bacteria will be visible on the slide at all
options.C: Only the Gram-negative bacteria will be visible
options.D: All bacteria will appear purple

explanation: Without the alcohol wash to strip the crystal violet out of thin cell walls, all cells keep the initial purple stain regardless of their actual type. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T3#BMP116_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why does a history of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease increase the risk of ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Scarred and narrowed fallopian tubes trap the fertilized egg before it reaches the uterus
options.B: Hormonal changes from the infection cause the embryo to multiply at twice the normal rate
options.C: The ovaries release fertilized eggs directly into the abdominal cavity instead of the tubes
options.D: The uterine lining becomes too thick for a normal embryo to successfully attach

explanation: Damaged tubular pathways prevent the smooth transit of the fertilized ovum, causing it to implant abnormally in the tube tissue. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T9#BMP310_U3_T9_h4)

question: How does the internal structure of a short bone differ from that of a long bone?

options.A: Short bones have a much thicker outer shell of cortical bone
options.B: Short bones contain only yellow marrow throughout their core
options.C: Short bones do not have any compact bone on the outside
options.D: Short bones lack a medullary cavity filled with yellow marrow

explanation: Long bones feature a distinct central medullary cavity, whereas short bones have a solid core of spongy bone enclosed by a thin compact shell. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T4#BMP111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the average measurement of the transverse diameter of the pelvic brim?

options.B: 13 cm
options.D: 11 cm

explanation: The transverse diameter is the widest transverse span of the pelvic brim, measuring roughly 13 centimetres. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h2)

question: An adult patient presents with fever, rust-colored sputum, and sharp chest pain when breathing. What initial imaging test should the midwife expect?

options.A: Chest radiograph
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Abdominal ultrasound
options.D: Computed tomography scan of the head

explanation: A chest X-ray is the standard, accessible imaging tool used to confirm fluid and consolidation in the lungs. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T6#BMP125_U1_T6_h3)

question: A patient receiving an anticholinergic medication has difficulty passing urine. Which action caused this?

options.A: Complete failure of the kidneys to produce urine
options.B: Sudden enlargement of the prostate gland
options.C: Relaxation of the bladder detrusor muscle
options.D: Strong contraction of the urethral sphincter

explanation: Anticholinergics relax the bladder muscle, making it hard for the patient to void, which results in urinary retention. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T5#BMP124_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of writing an incident report after a near-miss occurs?

options.A: To gather evidence that proves which staff member was lazy
options.B: To increase the hospital fees charged to the patient
options.C: To make sure the nurse involved gets suspended from work
options.D: To learn from system flaws and improve future patient safety

explanation: Incident reports help hospitals spot weak spots in their systems so they can fix them before real harm happens. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why must midwives tell the difference between iatrogenic infections and standard sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: They always present with much milder symptoms than other infections.
options.B: They do not involve bacteria or other microbial pathogens.
options.C: They arise from healthcare interventions rather than sexual exposure.
options.D: They resolve completely without the need for medical intervention.

explanation: Identifying the healthcare-related origin helps target infection control practices in the clinic. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T2#BMP310_U2_T2_h1)

question: According to Erik Erikson, what is the core psychosocial conflict that defines the adolescent life stage?

options.A: Trust versus Mistrust
options.B: Initiative versus Guilt
options.C: Generativity versus Stagnation
options.D: Identity versus Role Confusion

explanation: Erikson identified the central task of adolescence as figuring out who one is and where one fits into society, termed identity versus role confusion. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T1#BMP320_U3_T1_h5)

question: How do Community Health Committees help improve local health facilities?

options.A: By closing down clinics that do not meet international standards
options.B: By taking over the daily clinical duties of the resident midwives
options.C: By mobilizing community support for maintenance and resolving staff-patient grievances
options.D: By preventing community members from visiting formal hospitals

explanation: CHCs act as administrators and peacebuilders, keeping clinics functional and fostering good relationships. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T4#BMP117_U2_T4_h2)

question: How can a midwife in a rural Nigerian clinic actively support the National Population Policy?

options.A: Waiting exclusively for clients to ask for birth control without offering advice
options.B: Refusing to offer family planning services to young or unmarried women
options.C: Directing all pregnant women to travel abroad for routine antenatal care
options.D: Providing accurate contraceptive counseling and community health education

explanation: Educating clients and providing accessible, respectful family planning services directly helps reduce maternal mortality and supports healthy child spacing. [learn more](BMP224_U1_T2#BMP224_U1_T2_h5)

question: A breastfeeding mother has deep, shooting breast pain during feeds, and her nipples look shiny and pink. What condition should you suspect?

options.A: Bacterial cellulitis of the breast skin
options.B: Normal postpartum milk letdown reflex
options.C: A blocked milk duct with early abscess
options.D: Candidal mastitis of the nipple

explanation: Shiny, pink nipples with deep shooting pain during and after breastfeeding point toward a fungal yeast infection of the breast. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T8#BMP124_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is the risk of uterine infection significantly increased in a neglected shoulder presentation?

options.A: Maternal white blood cells are completely suppressed
options.B: The transverse position attracts local skin pathogens
options.C: Prolonged rupture of membranes allows bacteria to ascend
options.D: The fetal skin produces inflammatory toxins in utero

explanation: When membranes stay ruptured for a long time during obstructed labor, bacteria easily travel up into the uterine cavity. [learn more](BMP311_U1_T4#BMP311_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which condition involves the halt of multiple ovarian follicles before a dominant one can form?

options.A: Cervical ectropion
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.D: Pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome involves hormonal imbalances that stop normal follicle development, leaving many small arrested follicles in the ovaries. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T4#BMP210_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is treating worm infections especially important for pregnant women?

options.A: Worm burdens interfere with routine ultrasound scans
options.B: Parasites worsen maternal anaemia by stealing vital nutrients
options.C: Helminths directly trigger premature labour contractions
options.D: Worms cause high blood sugar levels during pregnancy

explanation: Worms consume essential nutrients and cause blood loss, which increases the risk of dangerous anaemia during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T10#BMP124_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why is expressed breastmilk especially critical for the management of preterm infants in the neonatal unit?

options.A: Preterm infants cannot tolerate artificial milk formulas under any clinical circumstances
options.B: It provides specialized immunological protection and is easier for their immature gut to digest
options.C: It contains higher amounts of water to prevent dehydration caused by radiant warmers
options.D: Expressed milk eliminates the need for any vitamin or mineral supplementation

explanation: Preterm infants have fragile digestive systems and benefit immensely from the protective properties and easy digestibility of human milk. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h6)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with severe throat pain, fever, swollen neck glands, and white spots on the tonsils, but no cough. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Viral bronchitis
options.B: Fungal stomatitis
options.C: Allergic rhinitis
options.D: Bacterial pharyngitis

explanation: The cluster of high fever, white spots on the tonsils, and lack of a cough points directly toward streptococcal bacterial pharyngitis. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T4#BMP125_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of soaking bloody delivery instruments in 0.5 percent chlorine solution immediately after use?

options.A: Softening the metal to make manual scrubbing much easier
options.B: Decontamination to neutralize dangerous blood-borne pathogens
options.C: Removal of grease and rust from aging surgical metal
options.D: Final sterilization so they are ready for the next patient

explanation: Decontamination is an initial step that makes handling safer for cleaning staff and kills fragile viruses before they dry. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary infection-control practice when performing a vaginal examination in labor?

options.A: Changing the examination table paper between patients
options.B: Wiping the perineum from back to front afterward
options.C: Applying warm water and perfumed soap beforehand
options.D: Using sterile gloves and clean antiseptic technique

explanation: Strict asepsis prevents introducing bacteria into the birth canal, which can lead to severe uterine infections. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h5)

question: What key feature should a midwife look for when reviewing a mixed-methods research paper?

options.A: A guarantee that the research cost a lot of money
options.B: The use of complex foreign words in every paragraph
options.C: True integration of both quantitative and qualitative data
options.D: An absence of any tables, charts, or statistical numbers

explanation: A good mixed-methods study goes beyond listing two methods; it integrates them to answer the research question thoroughly. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T4#BMP225_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which part of the blood increases the most during pregnancy, leading to hemodilution?

options.A: Platelets
options.B: Plasma
options.C: White blood cells
options.D: Red blood cells

explanation: Plasma volume increases much faster than red blood cell mass during pregnancy, diluting the blood concentration and leading to physiological anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T4#BMP118_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is proper antimalarial drug use particularly critical within the Nigerian healthcare system?

options.A: It eliminates the need for mosquito nets
options.B: It guarantees immunity against future bites
options.C: It prevents widespread drug resistance
options.D: It shortens hospital stays to one day

explanation: Using antimalarial drugs correctly and only when necessary stops the parasite from mutating and becoming immune to standard treatments. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T12#BMP124_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is a catheter used to empty the urinary bladder right before an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: To stimulate regular uterine contractions during the surgery
options.B: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid produced
options.C: To eliminate the need for any post-operative urine monitoring
options.D: To prevent accidental surgical injury to the bladder

explanation: An empty bladder moves away from the lower uterine segment, lowering the chance of it being accidentally cut during the surgery. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that the placenta has separated?

options.A: Continuous severe lower abdominal pain
options.B: A sudden gush of dark blood from the vagina
options.C: Lengthening of the visible umbilical cord
options.D: The uterus changing to a globular shape

explanation: Severe continuous pain is a sign of complications like abruption or rupture, not normal physiological placental separation. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major advantage of observational studies in healthcare?

options.A: They are often the only practical way to study rare diseases
options.B: They reflect normal, everyday clinical practices and patient behaviors
options.C: They can prove absolute causation without any possibility of error
options.D: They are ethical to use when testing harmful exposures is forbidden

explanation: Observational studies struggle to prove absolute causation due to confounding variables and biases, making option A the incorrect statement. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T3#BMP225_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is a full bladder often recommended for a transabdominal scan during early pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling dizzy during the test
options.B: It stimulates active fetal movements for easier counting
options.C: It pushes the uterus upward for better visualization
options.D: It measures the exact renal function of the mother

explanation: A full urinary bladder acts as an acoustic window and elevates the early pregnant uterus out of the pelvic cavity so the sonographer can see it clearly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason women get bladder infections (cystitis) more often than men?

options.A: A shorter urethra close to the anus
options.B: Lower pelvic floor muscle tone
options.C: Increased bladder sensitivity to urine
options.D: A larger bladder capacity overall

explanation: The female urethra is short and sits very close to the anus, which means bacteria have a much shorter distance to travel to reach the bladder. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T3#BMP216_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the recommended initial action when a breastfeeding mother is prescribed a new medication?

options.A: Advise the mother to permanently wean her baby immediately
options.B: Switch the baby to full formula feeding without checking guidelines
options.C: Tell her to discard all expressed milk for the next two weeks
options.D: Consult a verified reference guide on drug safety during lactation

explanation: Most medications are safe during breastfeeding, so midwives must check reliable drug reference sources rather than automatically stopping breastfeeding. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T2#BMP212_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why does the human body need a complex control system for breathing instead of just a simple fixed rhythm?

options.A: The lungs constantly change in size and shape.
options.B: Skeletal muscles tire out very quickly at rest.
options.C: Atmospheric pressure varies throughout the day.
options.D: Metabolic demands and activity levels constantly change.

explanation: The body needs a flexible system to adjust breathing depth and rate depending on whether a person is resting, active, or fighting an infection. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T5#BMP121_U1_T5_h1)

question: How many times a day should a breastfed baby aged 6 to 8 months usually get solid meals?

options.A: 6 to 8 times daily
options.B: 2 to 3 times daily
options.C: Only when crying
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Guidelines recommend offering solid foods 2 to 3 times a day alongside breast milk for infants aged 6 to 8 months. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T3#BMP118_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary reason pregnant women are more vulnerable to malaria infections?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies common in the tropics
options.B: Higher exposure to mosquito bites at night
options.C: An increase in overall blood volume
options.D: Temporary changes in their immune system

explanation: Pregnancy naturally lowers certain immune responses, which makes it harder for a woman's body to fight off malaria parasites effectively. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T5#BMP221_U4_T5_h1)

question: Who is ultimately responsible for patient care when a task is delegated to a junior worker?

options.A: The patient receiving the treatment in the ward
options.B: The professional nurse or midwife who delegated the task
options.C: The junior worker who performed the physical action
options.D: The hospital administrator who signed the employment form

explanation: While the junior worker performs the task, the professional nurse remains accountable for the overall outcome. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T5#BMP120_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the term for the oxygen debt the body repays after intense exercise?

options.A: Myometrial recovery perfusion index
options.B: Anaerobic threshold saturation level
options.C: Excess post-exercise oxygen consumption
options.D: Cardiorespiratory minute ventilation rate

explanation: EPOC is the term for the extra oxygen the body takes in after exertion to restore normal balance. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T6#BMP111_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of giving Anti-D immunoglobulin to a Rhesus-negative pregnant woman?

options.A: To stimulate the immediate production of maternal breast milk
options.B: To lower high maternal blood pressure during the third trimester
options.C: To prevent her immune system from forming antibodies against fetal red blood cells
options.D: To cure existing bacterial infections within the amniotic fluid cavity

explanation: Anti-D immunoglobulin clears any fetal Rhesus-positive cells that enter the mother's circulation before her immune system reacts to them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T11#BMP111_U6_T11_h6)

question: Which visual sign in a fresh urine sample should alert a midwife to a possible urinary tract infection?

options.A: Cloudiness with visible floating particles
options.B: A faint, slightly aromatic scent
options.C: A pale yellow and transparent appearance
options.D: A high volume of total output

explanation: Cloudy urine often contains pus, bacteria, and cellular debris which are signs of inflammation or infection in the urinary tract. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h5)

question: A team member receives an instruction to give magnesium sulfate. What is the correct response in a closed-loop system?

options.A: Nod silently and begin searching for a syringe in the medication trolley
options.B: Ask another colleague if they think the dose is appropriate
options.C: Wait until the procedure is fully completed before speaking
options.D: Repeat the medication name and dose back to the leader immediately

explanation: The receiver must verbally repeat the order back to confirm correct understanding before carrying it out. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h3)

options.A: To increase the cost of healthcare for rural dwellers
options.B: To reduce the number of patients visiting any hospital
options.C: To punish health workers who make mistakes
options.D: To transfer complicated cases to higher-level facilities

explanation: Referrals ensure patients who need advanced medical or surgical care are moved safely to a hospital equipped to handle them. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h7)

question: A midwife finishes repairing an episiotomy and places the bloody forceps directly onto a dry tray without wiping them. What is the main risk of this action?

options.A: The blood will dry and form a protective layer over trapped bacteria
options.B: The forceps will lose their metal temper from the air exposure
options.C: The instruments will rust before they reach the washing sink
options.D: The hospital will run out of clean trays too quickly

explanation: Dried blood hardens on surfaces, protecting underlying microorganisms from being reached by cleaning agents and sterilizing gases or steam. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h2)

question: A pregnant woman has active genital herpes near her delivery date. What is the main concern for the baby?

options.A: Immediate need to administer high doses of routine bacterial antibiotics
options.B: Permanent immunity for the infant against all viral respiratory infections
options.C: Certain development of congenital hearing loss in the unborn baby
options.D: Risk of transmitting the virus to the newborn during a vaginal birth

explanation: Active herpes lesions during labor pose a risk of passing the virus to the baby, which is why precautions like a cesarean section are often considered. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T2#BMP116_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why do young children lose body water much faster than adults when they are sick?

options.A: They naturally consume more salt in their regular daily meals
options.B: Their kidneys are fully mature and flush out water too quickly
options.C: They sweat less often, trapping heat inside their bodies
options.D: They have a higher body water percentage and surface-area-to-mass ratio

explanation: A larger surface area relative to body size means children lose fluids and electrolytes much faster through the skin and respiratory tract. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T4#BMP118_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important to follow the exact timing instructions when reading reagent strips?

options.A: Color reactions keep changing over time, leading to wrong results if read too late
options.B: The plastic strip will dissolve if left in the air too long
options.C: It prevents the patient from seeing their test results
options.D: The urine sample cools down and stops the chemical reaction completely

explanation: The chemical pads change color progressively over seconds and minutes, so reading them at the wrong time gives inaccurate results. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h6)

question: A mother shares that her newborn cries frantically and refuses to latch. What advice should you give based on rooting behavior?

options.A: Stop breastfeeding entirely and switch straight to artificial formula
options.B: Wait until the baby is completely exhausted so it will sleep at the breast
options.C: Look for early rooting cues like head turning before the baby starts crying
options.D: Force the baby's mouth open immediately regardless of head movement

explanation: Spotting early feeding cues keeps the baby calm and prevents them from getting overtired, making it much easier to latch. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h6)

question: A ward manager notices high rates of incomplete partographs and holds a quick refresher session on proper plotting. Which management function does this represent?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Organizing
options.C: Staffing
options.D: Controlling

explanation: Reviewing documentation standards and correcting performance gaps through training is a classic example of controlling. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T5#BMP312_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which meal plan is a good example of a balanced local diet for an antenatal client in Nigeria?

options.A: A large bowl of white rice eaten completely plain with water
options.B: Fried dough snacks paired with a bottled sugary carbonated drink
options.C: Only roasted maize consumed throughout the entire morning
options.D: Eba with egusi soup, fish, and a side of steamed spinach

explanation: This meal combines carbohydrates, protein, fats, and protective vitamins from vegetables into a balanced dish. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is relying solely on short-term international donor grants dangerous for health program sustainability?

options.A: Foreign grants automatically eliminate all cultural barriers
options.B: Donors always force health workers to close down schools permanently
options.C: International money cannot be converted into local Nigerian currency
options.D: Programs may collapse abruptly when the donor funding cycle ends

explanation: Sustainable programs require local ownership and domestic budget integration so they continue running after external partners leave. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T6#BMP320_U3_T6_h6)

question: What should a midwife do if an ongoing community health intervention fails to meet its targets?

options.A: Hand over all clinical responsibilities to traditional healers
options.B: Blame the villagers for being uncooperative and stop all visits
options.C: Falsify the clinic records to make the program look successful
options.D: Reconvene with the community to review and adjust the strategy together

explanation: Community-centred care relies on collaboration, meaning challenges are addressed as a team through participatory problem-solving. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T10#BMP110_U5_T10_h6)

question: Which two regions of the human skeleton contain short bones?

options.A: Skull and spine
options.B: Ribcage and pelvis
options.C: Shoulder and thigh
options.D: Wrist and ankle

explanation: Short bones are found exclusively in the carpals of the wrist and the tarsals of the ankle. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T4#BMP111_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of managing varicose veins conservatively during pregnancy?

options.A: To improve blood flow back to the heart and relieve discomfort
options.B: To prevent the uterus from pressing on the spine
options.C: To permanently cure faulty valves inside deep veins
options.D: To completely stop the increase in maternal blood volume

explanation: Because pregnancy changes are temporary, conservative care focuses on helping blood flow upward to ease pain and swelling. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T14#BMP212_U1_T14_h5)

question: What is the very first thing that forms inside a fresh bone break within the first few days?

options.A: A thick layer of scar skin
options.B: A permanent steel plate
options.C: A blood clot hematoma
options.D: A hard compact shell

explanation: Blood vessels break during a fracture, and the resulting bleeding pools around the ends to form an initial protective hematoma. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T2#BMP216_U3_T2_h2)

question: A newborn baby shows unsteady movements and poor muscle control. Which brain area is likely still developing or affected?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The cerebrum
options.C: The dura mater
options.D: The spinal nerves

explanation: Because the cerebellum coordinates movement and balance, issues in this region often show up as uncoordinated physical activity in infants. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T2#BMP121_U5_T2_h3)

question: What percentage of pre-pregnancy weight loss is considered a warning sign in early pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Five percent
options.B: Fifteen percent
options.C: Twenty percent
options.D: Ten percent

explanation: Losing more than five percent of body weight signals that vomiting is becoming severe enough to impact maternal health and nutritional status. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h3)

question: A patient arrives with obstructed labor, a baby that has passed away, and signs of an impending uterine rupture. Why might an evisceration be considered instead of a Caesarean section?

options.A: The hospital has an advanced neonatal intensive care unit
options.B: The first stage of labor is entirely normal and uncomplicated
options.C: The family explicitly asked to avoid any abdominal surgery
options.D: Abdominal surgery poses an extreme risk of death for an exhausted, infected mother

explanation: When a Caesarean section carries a very high risk of maternal death due to severe infection or impending rupture, clearing the birth canal vaginally may be weighed. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T7#BMP311_U3_T7_h2)

question: What action is required under IMCI guidelines when a child's condition is classified in the Pink category?

options.A: Discharge with nutritional counseling only
options.B: Routine follow-up visit after one week
options.C: Simple home management and reassurance
options.D: Urgent pre-referral treatment and hospital transfer

explanation: The pink row represents a severe classification, demanding emergency pre-referral treatment and transfer to a higher facility. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h5)

question: A pregnant woman eats a meal of beans and spinach. Which food item should a midwife suggest she consume alongside this meal to greatly improve iron absorption?

options.A: Strong local black tea without milk
options.B: Fresh orange juice containing vitamin C
options.C: Unrefined sorghum with high phytate levels
options.D: Cold whole cow's milk high in calcium

explanation: Vitamin C significantly enhances the absorption of non-heme plant iron in the gut, whereas tea, phytates, and calcium can inhibit it. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T9#BMP118_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why do opportunistic fungal infections rarely cause severe disease in healthy people?

options.A: Normal bacterial flora actively kills all fungal spores
options.B: An intact immune system successfully controls the organism
options.C: Body temperature is too high for opportunistic fungi to survive
options.D: Healthy skin tissues produce natural antifungal oils

explanation: Opportunistic fungi are weak pathogens that require a compromised immune system or disrupted body defenses to establish deep or widespread infection. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T2#BMP116_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is considered unsafe practice when giving labor-stimulating drugs?

options.A: Giving oxytocin without checking for cephalopelvic disproportion
options.B: Monitoring maternal blood pressure and pulse during resuscitation
options.C: Plotting cervical dilation on an active partograph hourly
options.D: Counseling previous caesarean scar mothers to deliver in hospital

explanation: Giving oxytocin when there is a physical blockage to the baby passing forces the uterus to contract against an obstruction, raising the risk of rupture. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T4#BMP311_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which layer of the hair shaft contains the pigment melanin that gives hair its color?

options.A: The medulla
options.B: The cortex
options.C: The dermal papilla
options.D: The cuticle

explanation: The cortex is the middle layer of the hair shaft and holds the pigment granules responsible for hair color along with structural strength. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T8#BMP111_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why are tiny bones like the phalanges in the fingers classified as long bones?

options.A: They contain no spongy bone tissue at any stage of life
options.B: They do not connect to any skeletal muscles
options.C: They share the same basic internal structural pattern as larger limbs
options.D: They grow exclusively through intramembranous ossification

explanation: Bones are classified based on their internal structural design rather than their absolute size. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T3#BMP111_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the best way to confirm that an endotracheal tube is placed correctly in the trachea?

options.A: Hearing air escaping around the edges of the lips
options.B: Observing immediate pinking of the infant's skin
options.C: Noticing gastric distention in the upper abdomen
options.D: Detecting exhaled carbon dioxide and symmetrical breath sounds

explanation: Carbon dioxide detectors and hearing breath sounds equally on both sides confirm the tube is in the windpipe and not the stomach. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of non-probability sampling?

options.A: It is impossible to conduct interviews with the participants
options.B: Ethical boards automatically reject all non-random studies
options.C: Results cannot be safely generalized to the wider population
options.D: It requires massive financial budgets and computer software

explanation: Because participants are not chosen randomly, the findings apply only to the specific group studied rather than the general public. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T6#BMP225_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is a sperm cell built so differently from an egg cell?

options.A: Eggs need tails to swim toward the sperm
options.B: Sperm need large amounts of cytoplasm to survive
options.C: Sperm contain multiple nuclei for cell fusion
options.D: Sperm are built for swimming, while eggs store nutrients for growth

explanation: A sperm sheds most of its cytoplasm to stay light and fast for travel, while an egg keeps its cytoplasm to feed the early embryo. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T1#BMP210_U4_T1_h4)

question: How do fibrous joints behave when subjected to excessive mechanical force beyond their normal limits?

options.A: They temporarily convert into synovial joints
options.B: They expand to absorb the force safely
options.C: They slide smoothly into a new permanent position
options.D: They suffer structural tearing or injury

explanation: Because they lack a joint cavity and wide range of motion, extreme force on a fibrous joint results in ligament tears or bone fracture rather than normal movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T14#BMP111_U2_T14_h5)

question: Which warning sign should a midwife tell a patient with a cerclage to report right away?

options.A: Mild morning sickness and food cravings
options.B: Darkening of the skin line on the belly
options.C: Gentle baby kicks felt in the abdomen
options.D: New pelvic pressure or fluid leaking

explanation: Pelvic pressure or fluid leakage can mean the stitch is failing, membranes are bulging, or labor is starting, which needs immediate medical attention. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why is relying on a variety of local whole foods better than taking isolated supplements alone?

options.A: Whole foods provide a balanced mix of multiple vitamins, minerals, and fiber together.
options.B: Supplements are completely illegal to buy or sell in local Nigerian markets.
options.C: Whole foods contain heavy amounts of artificial preservatives for energy.
options.D: Synthetic vitamins cannot be absorbed by the human digestive tract at all.

explanation: Dietary variety ensures the pregnant woman receives synergistic nutrients that work together for optimal health. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T5#BMP118_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous for a patient to stop taking their prescribed antibiotics halfway through just because their abdominal pain has disappeared?

options.A: The remaining pills will turn poisonous if left sitting in the bottle
options.B: The stomach acid will instantly burn a hole through the duodenum
options.C: The bacterial infection may return stronger and develop drug resistance
options.D: The patient will immediately start vomiting dark coffee-ground blood

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early fails to eradicate the bacteria completely, allowing surviving microbes to multiply and develop drug resistance. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T5#BMP125_U3_T5_h8)

question: Which skin layer relies entirely on the dermal blood supply for its nourishment?

options.A: Epidermis
options.B: Subcutaneous layer
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Adipose layer

explanation: The epidermis lacks blood vessels of its own, so it depends on diffusion from the capillary loops in the dermal papillary layer. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T2#BMP111_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT part of the initial midwife assessment for a woman who might be in labor?

options.A: Surgically repairing the perineum
options.B: Evaluating contraction patterns
options.C: Assessing maternal vital signs
options.D: Checking fetal heart tones

explanation: Perineal repair is done after the baby is born, not during the first assessment of someone who may be in labor. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T2#BMP212_U2_T2_h5)

question: A patient receiving a salbutamol infusion suddenly has a pulse rate of 130 beats per minute. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Reduce or stop the infusion and notify the doctor
options.B: Administer a painkiller for a headache
options.C: Increase the drip rate to flush the drug out faster
options.D: Give her a cold drink of water and tell her to relax

explanation: A heart rate above safe limits means the drug dose is too high, requiring an immediate reduction or halt to protect the mother's heart. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following physical findings is typically observed in a patient experiencing early shock?

options.A: Flushed, warm, and dry skin
options.B: Cool, pale, and clammy skin
options.C: Bounding and very strong pulse
options.D: Slow and deep respiratory pattern

explanation: Peripheral vasoconstriction shunts blood away from the skin, making it feel cool, pale, and clammy. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T4#BMP110_U7_T4_h4)

question: Why is it important to note recent antibiotic use on the laboratory request form?

options.A: It helps the laboratory calculate the exact weight of the stool
options.B: It proves the patient is paying for their diagnostic tests
options.C: Laboratories require drug receipts for insurance claims
options.D: Antibiotics can alter the growth of bacteria in stool cultures

explanation: Medications like antibiotics suppress normal or abnormal flora, which directly affects how the laboratory interprets culture results. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T7#BMP110_U6_T7_h6)

question: What is the correct action when a midwife is analyzing raw community health data?

options.A: Organize and compare the numbers against targets or past records to find gaps
options.B: Change the figures to match the expectations of local politicians
options.C: Destroy all records that show poor health outcomes in the district
options.D: Hide the results so that community members do not panic

explanation: Analyzing data means organizing the raw numbers and comparing them to past records or goals to spot actual health issues. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T2#BMP117_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which major ligament runs down the front of the vertebral bodies to prevent excessive backward bending?

options.A: Ligamentum flavum
options.B: Supraspinous ligament
options.C: Anterior longitudinal ligament
options.D: Posterior longitudinal ligament

explanation: The anterior longitudinal ligament is wide and stout, securing the front of the spinal column against hyperextension. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T8#BMP111_U2_T8_h5)

question: What dangerous condition must you always rule out when a woman has early bleeding and severe pelvic pain?

options.A: Normal twin delivery
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy can look like a normal early bleed but can cause life-threatening internal bleeding if missed. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T1#BMP221_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a major benefit of using centralized hospital kitchens in maternity wards?

options.A: Guaranteed preference for local traditional recipes by patients
options.B: Complete elimination of the need for nursing supervision
options.C: Precise control over therapeutic diet portions and nutrients
options.D: Elimination of all delays in food delivery during emergencies

explanation: Central kitchens can measure exact ingredients, making it much easier to follow doctor orders for specialized diets. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T8#BMP118_U4_T8_h4)

question: How do routine health education sessions during antenatal care directly improve pregnancy outcomes?

options.A: By empowering women to recognize complications early and adopt healthy lifestyle habits
options.B: By eliminating all common minor disorders of pregnancy automatically
options.C: By guaranteeing that the baby will be born on the exact estimated due date
options.D: By replacing the need for laboratory blood investigations

explanation: Education equips mothers with knowledge to take preventive actions and seek prompt help when danger signs occur. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T9#BMP212_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why is close monitoring needed after giving naloxone?

options.A: Naloxone causes severe allergic reactions exactly one hour after injection
options.B: It causes the blood pressure to drop to zero without warning
options.C: The patient will immediately fall into a permanent coma once the drug takes effect
options.D: Naloxone wears off faster than many opioids, allowing breathing depression to return

explanation: Because naloxone has a short half-life, its reversal effects fade before long-acting opioids clear, risking a return of dangerous symptoms. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h6)

question: What finding under a microscope is a key sign of bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Gram-negative diplococci
options.B: Motile trichomonads
options.C: Clue cells
options.D: Fungal hyphae

explanation: Clue cells are vaginal skin cells covered in so many bacteria that their edges look fuzzy and unclear, which points to bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: A Muslim couple experiences a stillbirth in a hospital. What is an essential practical step for the midwifery team?

options.A: Facilitate prompt religious rites and quick discharge according to their faith
options.B: Insist the body remains in the mortuary for a two-week investigation
options.C: Tell the family crying is prohibited
options.D: Ignore religious preferences and follow standard discharge times

explanation: Islamic tradition encourages prompt burial and spiritual rites, making quick coordination by the healthcare team essential. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is one of the strongest predictors of preterm labor?

options.A: Having a history of prolonged post-term labor
options.B: Eating a high-protein diet
options.C: Having O-negative blood group
options.D: Having a history of a previous preterm birth

explanation: A woman who has had a prior preterm delivery has a much higher chance of experiencing it again in future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T1#BMP311_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which finding during a community check means you should escalate to emergency care right away?

options.A: Normal weight gain observed across two consecutive monthly visits
options.B: Fetal heart sounds heard clearly through a standard pinard stethoscope
options.C: A persistent blood pressure reading of 140/90 mmHg or higher
options.D: A mild and normal feeling of fatigue at the end of the day

explanation: Elevated blood pressure is a critical warning sign for pre-eclampsia, which requires prompt medical evaluation and potential hospital referral. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T2#BMP215_U2_T2_h4)

question: How often should vital signs be checked in the immediate recovery phase after ECT?

options.A: Continuously for exactly twenty-four hours
options.B: Once every four hours overnight
options.C: Only when the patient reports chest pain
options.D: Every fifteen minutes until stable

explanation: Frequent checks every fifteen minutes help nurses catch sudden blood pressure or breathing shifts early in recovery. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T5#BMP223_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which part of the spleen is mainly responsible for fighting infections?

options.A: The red pulp
options.B: The splenic capsule
options.C: The white pulp
options.D: The trabeculae

explanation: The white pulp contains special immune cells that help the body fight off germs found in the blood. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T2#BMP111_U6_T2_h2)

question: According to Taylor, who should be primarily responsible for planning how work is done?

options.A: The workers
options.B: External auditors
options.C: Government regulators
options.D: Management

explanation: Taylor's principles set a clear division where managers handle the planning while staff focus on carrying out the tasks. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T3#BMP312_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is a key nursing priority right after a patient undergoes an evisceration?

options.A: Discharging the patient within two hours to save hospital space
options.B: Starting immediate breastfeeding training
options.C: Encouraging physical exercise to prevent blood clots
options.D: Monitoring closely for heavy bleeding and signs of infection

explanation: Because the procedure follows prolonged and difficult labor, watching for postpartum hemorrhage and sepsis is critical for saving the mother's life. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T7#BMP311_U3_T7_h6)

question: Why does a history of a previous vertical (classical) cesarean section mean prostaglandins should not be used?

options.A: The vertical upper uterine scar has a very high risk of tearing apart under strong contractions
options.B: The muscular wall becomes completely paralyzed and will never contract again
options.C: Prostaglandins interact dangerously with old scar tissue and cause permanent nerve damage
options.D: The previous surgical incision prevents the cervix from ever producing any collagen

explanation: Vertical scars in the upper part of the uterus are weak points that can easily rupture when powerful labor medications are introduced. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T8#BMP213_U1_T8_h7)

question: Why do bony growths called osteophytes form around joints in late-stage osteoarthritis?

options.A: Muscles around the joint contract tightly and pull the bone outward.
options.B: Chronic bacterial infection triggers excessive calcium deposits.
options.C: Synovial membranes overproduce thick fluid to lubricate bones.
options.D: The body attempts to repair joint damage caused by cartilage loss.

explanation: Bone spurs form because the body tries to stabilize a joint after it loses its protective cartilage cushioning. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why does IMCI use symptom-based color-coded charts instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: To replace the need for physical examination by trained health workers
options.B: To prove that laboratory testing is entirely unnecessary in clinics
options.C: To reduce the paperwork required for clinic record books
options.D: To enable rapid life-saving treatment decisions in resource-limited settings

explanation: Many primary clinics lack functional labs, so IMCI uses physical signs to guide urgent action immediately. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following describes the principle of woman-centred care?

options.A: Following strict hospital routines regardless of individual patient wishes
options.B: Placing the mother's personal values and needs at the center of decisions
options.C: Allowing the obstetrician to make all final choices without patient input
options.D: Prioritizing hospital administrative efficiency over maternal comfort

explanation: Woman-centred care means respecting the unique background, beliefs, and choices of the mother rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all routine. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why do pregnant women with asthma have less breathing reserve?

options.A: Their bodies consume more oxygen while functional residual capacity decreases
options.B: Their lung tissue permanently shrinks during the first trimester
options.C: Pregnancy completely stops air from entering the bronchial tubes
options.D: Heart rates drop so low that oxygen cannot travel through the blood

explanation: Higher oxygen needs combined with less room in the chest cavity mean less reserve to draw on during an asthma flare-up. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T8#BMP125_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why does a poor infant latch frequently lead to the development of mastitis?

options.A: It forces the milk ducts to close permanently
options.B: It causes the baby to swallow excess air
options.C: It triggers an immediate allergic reaction in the skin
options.D: It leaves certain areas of the breast unemptied

explanation: When the baby does not latch well, milk is not removed evenly, leaving stagnant pools that can easily become inflamed or infected. [learn more](BMP214_U3_T6#BMP214_U3_T6_h2)

question: Why are extremely high-protein diets discouraged for patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: They stop diuretic medications from working.
options.B: They increase pressure inside the kidney filters and can worsen damage.
options.C: They stop the liver from producing cholesterol.
options.D: They cause an immediate drop in blood pressure.

explanation: Eating too much protein forces the kidneys to work harder, which can increase filtering pressure and speed up kidney decline. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main difference between CAPD and APD?

options.A: CAPD requires hospital admission for every exchange, while APD can be done anywhere outdoors.
options.B: CAPD filters blood through a machine, while APD only filters urine through the bladder.
options.C: CAPD uses a permanent blood pump, while APD relies entirely on natural kidney function.
options.D: CAPD is performed manually by the patient during the day, while APD uses a machine mostly at night.

explanation: CAPD stands for continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis, which is manual and done throughout the day, whereas APD uses a cycler machine overnight. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T9#BMP216_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main function of the denial stage after a sudden loss?

options.A: Permanently hiding the truth from family
options.B: Acting as a temporary buffer to protect the mind from overwhelming pain
options.C: Speeding up physical recovery
options.D: Punishing the healthcare team

explanation: Denial numbs immediate shock, giving the individual time to slowly process reality at their own pace. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the medical term for the natural loss of muscle mass that happens as people get older?

options.A: Atherosclerosis
options.B: Osteomalacia
options.C: Sarcopenia
options.D: Hypoglycemia

explanation: Sarcopenia describes the shrinking of muscle bulk and strength associated with aging, which lowers the body's overall energy needs. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T7#BMP118_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why should infertility and sexually transmitted infections be handled together in community care?

options.A: National health insurance only pays for both conditions if diagnosed on the exact same day
options.B: Patients refuse to discuss family planning unless both issues are addressed simultaneously
options.C: Unmanaged infections are a leading preventable cause of tubal damage and subsequent infertility
options.D: Midwives lack the training to treat reproductive tract infections without prior fertility testing

explanation: Many reproductive tract infections lead to pelvic inflammatory disease, which causes the structural blockages that can lead to infertility. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T8#BMP126_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why do health workers look at the whole child instead of treating just one symptom?

question: When are prophylactic antibiotics typically recommended for a patient with a complete abortion?

options.A: Only when the patient requests pain relief medications
options.B: Never under any circumstances in maternity care settings
options.C: Only if there are signs of infection such as fever or foul discharge
options.D: For every single patient regardless of their physical examination

options.A: Hospital budget constraints with personal salary desires

options.C: Male participants equally with female participants
options.D: Statistical needs with available resources and logistics

question: How can a midwife check if a solely breastfed newborn is getting enough milk?

options.A: By weighing the mother before and after each feeding session
options.B: By checking the frequency of wet diapers and infant weight gain
options.C: By testing the protein content of the mother's casual sweat
options.D: By measuring the exact duration of the baby's afternoon nap

explanation: Adequate urine output and steady weight gain are reliable clinical proof that the baby is taking in enough milk. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T4#BMP215_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which objective lens requires the use of a special oil to prevent light from bending?

options.A: The 10x low power lens
options.B: The scanning objective lens
options.C: The 100x oil immersion lens
options.D: The 40x high dry lens

explanation: The 100x lens needs oil to bridge the gap between the glass and the lens because oil has the same light-bending properties as glass. [learn more](BMP116_U1_T3#BMP116_U1_T3_h1)

question: What happens inside a healthy vein when surrounding skeletal muscles relax?

options.A: Valve flaps snap shut to prevent backward blood flow
options.B: The smooth muscle layer forces blood upward on its own
options.C: Venous valves open wide to let oxygen enter the vessel walls
options.D: Blood immediately rushes backward into the smaller capillaries

explanation: When muscles relax, gravity pulls blood downward, filling the valve pockets and forcing the flaps tightly closed so blood cannot flow backward. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T16#BMP111_U5_T16_h2)

question: During a vaginal exam, a midwife notices the baby's head is not flexing or turning as expected. Why is writing this down immediately so important?

options.A: To detect abnormal progress and intervene before complications arise.
options.B: To prevent the need for any further vaginal examinations.
options.C: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby before delivery.
options.D: To prove that the mother is not pushing hard enough during contractions.

explanation: Catching labor delays or unusual positioning early helps the midwife take action before the mother or baby faces serious distress. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T4#BMP212_U2_T4_h8)

question: Where do the coronary arteries that supply the heart muscle originate?

options.A: Base of the aorta
options.B: Left atrium
options.C: Superior vena cava
options.D: Pulmonary trunk

explanation: The right and left coronary arteries branch directly off the base of the aorta just above the aortic semilunar valve. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T10#BMP111_U5_T10_h5)
